name: two-ball-collision
description: Two balls served and autolaunched along the identical deterministic path, the second 195 ticks behind the first -- the trailing ball catches up and makes contact. Momentum transferred, no overlap, no sticking, separation never below one ball diameter (verified by the runner's onTick hook across the WHOLE run, not merely at checkpoints). Measured on Story 2.1c's orbit geometry: minimum centre separation 27.181 mm at tick 1582, against a 26.99 mm ball diameter -- a real contact with 0.191 mm of clearance, where the previous recording had 0.015 mm. The spacing was 319 ticks before this story; on the orbit's own longer path that spacing left the balls 53.389 mm apart at their closest, so the collision this golden exists to pin never happened.

notes: stateHash() hashes the whole game tree, which includes machine.deviceSlots -- this golden therefore freezes the LOOP-WRITTEN value of deviceSlots (sim/loop/index.ts:341-344, the live AD-7 violation tracked as DW-70) as part of its reference hash. If Story 2.5's fix is faithful the values will be identical and nothing breaks; if this golden ever breaks on deviceSlots alone, check DW-70 before assuming the physics changed. durationTicks shortened from 6000 to 3400 by Story 2.1a task 25 (DW-119 residual): the pre-fix col_wall_bottom_l/_r had a dead-flat top face that stranded a resting ball forever, so this golden's own two balls could safely stay in play for the full original 6000 ticks. The fix (a genuine slope toward the drain aperture) now lets a ball that ends up on that ledge actually reach bd_trough -- measured this pass, the lead ball (id 0) drains at tick 3636. That is DW-119 working as intended, not a regression, but it falls outside what this golden claims ("both balls survive to the end"), which was never about drain routing. 3400 keeps a comfortable margin after the last close-approach event (measured: rebound detected by tick 2929, minimum separation ~26.99 mm at tick 2999) and well before the tick-3636 drain, so the full collision claim (momentum transferred, no overlap, no sticking, both balls present) is still demonstrated in its entirety. Story 2.1b (2026-09-01): header.tableHash/assetHash refreshed against the completed shot-map registry and collision document (TABLE gains ~31 switches, 7 coils and bd_lock; the collision document gains ~27 col_ nodes), header.gameStart.tuning unchanged (no TUNING value moved). expectedHash/expectedGameStateHash moved: bd_lock adds a slots entry to every snapshot's machine.deviceSlots, changing GameState's own shape regardless of trajectory -- booted [true, true, true] under the then-unconditional fill(true) default, corrected to [false, false, false] by Story 2.1d (see that story's own note below); 'empty-slots' was never accurate for this pass. Rework iteration 2 (2026-09-01), correcting this note: the sentence that used to stand here -- blaming "Blender's alphabetical bpy.data.objects ordering" reshuffling existing nodes' own array positions, with an "order-sensitive broadphase" -- was investigated and found FALSE, twice: the collision document is alphabetically sorted throughout, so the ~28 new names interleave among the existing ones rather than reshuffling their relative order, and a document rebuilt with the rework's own wall-height and deflector changes reverted reproduces the two affected goldens bit-identically, ruling out node reordering as the mechanism. The TRUE cause of the two affected goldens' own trajectory divergence was not identified by either the implement pass or this rework; DW-53's wall-height change (col_wall_left/_top/_right/_lane now reaching the glass) and DW-58's col_lane_deflector removal were both tested and ruled out individually (each reproduces the divergence bit-identically when reverted alone). State plainly rather than guess further: the trajectory changed because the shot map's own regeneration changed the collision document in some way this investigation did not isolate -- not because of the specific mechanism previously claimed here. This golden's own recorded scenario was re-verified against the refreshed run and still holds at the recorded transitions/coilPrologue/durationTicks (byte-identical, untouched). Rework iteration 3 (2026-09-02): header.assetHash and expectedHash refreshed again (mechanical requirement -- the collision document changed, so a stale assetHash throws before any hash comparison runs; expectedGameStateHash is UNCHANGED, 7f04ca54). The golden's own claim -- "the second ball, 300 ticks behind, catches up and makes contact" -- depended on the OLD deflector/col_loop_top's own specific timing; measured this pass, the two balls no longer close to within one ball diameter inside the recorded 3400-tick window (minimum observed separation 60.96 mm, against the covering test's own 31.99 mm sanity floor). This is a DIRECT, mechanistically understood consequence of the DELIBERATE, REQUIRED deflector fix (task list items 1-3), not an unexplained ripple -- both balls physically pass through the exact geometry this rework re-shaped. Re-recording the hashes alone would have left a golden called two-ball-collision in which no collision occurs: green, and proving nothing about collisions. MEASURED EVIDENCE that a genuine collision now occurs at 320/340: minimum centre separation 27.00531 mm at tick 1626 -- 0.015 mm outside one ball diameter (26.99 mm) and 4.98 mm inside the covering test's own near-contact ceiling, with the no-overlap floor (26.936 mm, one diameter less the runner's 0.0540 mm sub-VU tolerance) never breached at any tick. Separation is monotonically DECREASING through tick 1626 and INCREASING from tick 1627, so the runner's own rebound detector fires at tick 1627 with a pre-rebound separation of 27.0053 mm. Both balls are still in play at tick 3400 (the first drain of the run is at tick 4573, 1173 ticks past the window), so durationTicks 3400 still keeps its stated margin: 1774 ticks after the close approach and well before any drain. expectedGameStateHash is UNCHANGED (7f04ca54) -- as this golden's PARITY_INERT entry says, its GameState carries no trace of a trajectory; expectedHash moved to 84114962.
